'''Kevin B. Ford''' (born 22 December 1967) is an American [[mathematician]] working in [[analytic number theory]].

==Education and career==

=== Early life ===
Ford received a [[Bachelor of Science]] in Computer Science and Mathematics in 1990 from the [[California State University, Chico]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Kevin Ford's CV |url=https://ford126.web.illinois.edu/cv.html |access-date=2025-05-23 |website=ford126.web.illinois.edu}}</ref> He then attended the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] (UIUC), where he completed his doctoral studies in 1994 under the supervision of [[Heini Halberstam]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name="MathGenealogy"/> His dissertation was titled ''The representation of numbers as sums of unlike powers''.<ref name="MathGenealogy"/> 

=== Early career (1994–2001) ===
From September 1994 to June 1995 he was at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2019-12-09 |title=Kevin Ford - Scholars {{!}} Institute for Advanced Study |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/kevin-ford |access-date=2025-05-23 |website=www.ias.edu |language=en}}</ref> He was then a postdoc at [[UT Austin]] until 1998, while also doing software development at the NASA [[Ames Research Center]] during the summers of 1997 and 1998.<ref name=":0" /> From 1998 to 2001, Ford was an assistant professor at the [[University of South Carolina, Columbia]].<ref name=":0" />

=== Professorship (2001–present) ===
He has been a [[professor]] in the department of mathematics of UIUC since 2001.<ref name=":0" /> In addition, he returned to IAS from September 2009 to June 2010,<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> was a research member at the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] in 2017,<ref name=":0" /> and was a visiting fellow at [[Magdalen College, Oxford]] in 2019.<ref name=":0" />

As of 2025, Ford has supervised eight PhD students, all at UIUC.<ref name="MathGenealogy"/>

==Research==
Ford's early work focused on the distribution of [[Euler's totient function]]. In 1998, he published a paper that studied in detail the range of this function and established that [[Carmichael's totient function conjecture]] is true for all integers up to <math>10^{10^{10}}</math>.<ref>
{{cite journal | title = The distribution of totients | first = Kevin | last = Ford | journal = Ramanujan Journal | volume = 2 | issue = 1–2 | pages = 67–151 | doi = 10.1023/A:1009761909132| year = 1998 | arxiv = 1104.3264 | s2cid = 6232638}}
</ref>
In 1999, he settled [[Sierpinski’s conjecture]] on [[Euler's totient function]].<ref>{{cite journal | url = http://annals.math.princeton.edu/articles/7954 | title = The number of solutions of ''φ''(''x'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;''m'' | first = Kevin | last = Ford | journal = Annals of Mathematics | volume = 150 | issue = 1 | pages = 283–311 | publisher = Princeton University and the Institute for Advanced Study | doi = 10.2307/121103 | year = 1999 | jstor = 121103 | access-date = 2019-04-19 | archive-date = 2013-09-24 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130924145941/http://annals.math.princeton.edu/articles/7954 | url-status = dead }}</ref>

In August 2014, Kevin Ford, in collaboration with [[Ben Green (mathematician)|Green]], [[Sergei Konyagin|Konyagin]] and [[Terence Tao|Tao]],<ref>{{cite journal | url = http://annals.math.princeton.edu/2016/183-3/p04 | title = Large gaps between consecutive primes | last1=Ford|first1=Kevin|last2=Green|first2=Ben|last3=Konyagin|first3=Sergei|last4=Tao|first4=Terence | journal = Annals of Mathematics | volume = 183 | issue = 3 | pages = 935–974 | doi = 10.4007/annals.2016.183.3.4 | year = 2016 | arxiv = 1408.4505 | s2cid = 16336889 }}</ref> resolved a [[Prime gap#Lower bounds|longstanding conjecture]] of [[Paul Erdős|Erdős]] on large gaps between primes, also proven independently by [[James Maynard (mathematician)|James Maynard]].<ref>{{cite journal | url = http://annals.math.princeton.edu/2016/183-3/p03 | title = Large gaps between primes | first = James | last = Maynard | journal = Annals of Mathematics | volume = 183 | issue = 3 | pages = 915–933 | publisher = Princeton University and the Institute for Advanced Study | doi = 10.4007/annals.2016.183.3.3 | year = 2016 | arxiv = 1408.5110 | s2cid = 119247836 }}</ref>
The five mathematicians were awarded for their work the largest Erdős prize ($10,000) ever offered.
<ref name="Mathematicians Make a Major Discovery About Prime Numbers">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.wired.com/2014/12/mathematicians-make-major-discovery-prime-numbers/|title=Mathematicians Make a Major Discovery About Prime Numbers|magazine=Wired|access-date=27 July 2015|first=Erica |last=Klarreich|date=22 December 2014}}</ref> In 2017, they improved their results in a joint paper.
<ref>{{cite journal | title = Long gaps between primes | first1 = Kevin| last1 = Ford | first2 = Ben | last2 = Green | first3 = Sergei | last3 = Konyagin | first4 = James | last4 = Maynard | first5 = Terence | last5 = Tao| journal = Journal of the American Mathematical Society |  volume = 31 | pages = 65–105 | doi = 10.1090/jams/876  | year = 2018 | doi-access = free | arxiv = 1412.5029 }}
</ref>

He is one of the namesakes of the [[Erdős–Tenenbaum–Ford constant]],<ref>{{cite journal|
first1=Florian|last1=Luca|first2=Carl|last2=Pomerance|author2-link=Carl Pomerance|title=On the range of Carmichael's universal-exponent function|journal=[[Acta Arithmetica]]|volume=162|year=2014|issue=3|pages=289–308|mr=3173026|doi=10.4064/aa162-3-6|url=https://math.dartmouth.edu/~carlp/rangeoflambda13.pdf}}</ref> named for his work using it in estimating the number of small integers that have divisors in a given interval.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Koukoulopoulos|first=Dimitris|arxiv=0905.0163|doi=10.1093/imrn/rnq045|issue=24|journal=[[International Mathematics Research Notices]]|mr=2739805|pages=4585–4627|title=Divisors of shifted primes|year=2010|volume=2010|s2cid=7503281}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 2013, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2017-11-03.</ref>
